⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Besides pieces like quilts and coverlets, I always say duvet covers are the best accessories to give a bedscape a bit more personality.
  • Industry observers note that to truly find the best of the best, I rounded up a group of writers and editors to test duvet covers from our favorite bedding brands—featuring muted, structured covers for minimalists and trendy colorways and patterns for maximalists.
  • If you’re still on the fence about what to go with for your bedroom, I also tapped AD PRO Directory designers to share what they look for in duvet covers, including materiality and design.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Besides pieces like quilts and coverlets, I always say duvet covers are the best accessories to give a bedscape a bit more personality. Take it from Ariel Kaye, founder of juggernaut bedding brand Parachute, who has filled her eclectic LA home with a range of duvet covers that span vibrant, breezy linens to neutral, crisp percales.

Industry observers note that to truly find the best of the best, I rounded up a group of writers and editors to test duvet covers from our favorite bedding brands—featuring muted, structured covers for minimalists and trendy colorways and patterns for maximalists. As for our top pick, we went with Boll & Branch’s Signature Hemmed Duvet Set since it’s organic, has a smooth and breathable feel, and comes in tons of prints and colors for easy styling.

If you’re still on the fence about what to go with for your bedroom, I also tapped AD PRO Directory designers to share what they look for in duvet covers, including materiality and design. Read below to create your dream bedscape this season.

For consistency, all prices listed reflect queen-size duvets unless otherwise noted, but up to king sizes are available for purchase from each brand.

Sources indicate that boll & Branch is one of AD’s favorite brands when it comes to bedding. With super soft sheets and other products made from 100% organic cotton, they have a heavy focus on sustainability and directly sourcing raw materials. The duvet cover follows suit, with long-staple cotton making for a durable piece of bedding that I’ve found is breathable enough for both hot and cold nights.

This organic-cotton duvet set can please pretty much anyone with a traditional bedroom. It has a tried-and-true cotton sateen material that gets softer with every wash, and designs—including subtle botanical prints—that are a must for anyone with classic taste. The earthy tones are great for a grounded bedroom too.

Bring the outdoors in with your styling by pairing one of Boll & Branch’s botanical prints with a textured linen sheet set.

According to recent reports, shop AD editors have stood behind Boll & Branch for years because of the brand’s sustainable business model and high-quality bedding. The signature cotton sheets have even earned a top spot in our best-of guides for the last five years. Just like these sheets, shopping producer Lauren Arzbaecher tells me that this Boll & Branch duvet cover’s sateen weave has a buttery soft texture. “The cotton is very smooth, and I maintained a comfortable temperature throughout the night even when bundled up underneath all my bedding,” she says. As a cold sleeper, Arzbeacher loves layering extra throws and blankets on top of her duvet, and she says this ultra-breathable material has all the “cuddly qualities” you’d want without making you overheat. Even better, the bedding is 100% organic, so you can rest knowing you’re not breathing in any harmful chemicals.

According to recent reports, this sateen duvet cover also has a zipper closure, so it’s a lot easier for Arzbaecher to slip her Manufacturer Store down insert on and off than other button-closure covers she’s tried. “Their solid color range has a lovely mix of earthy hues, and the brand has been releasing more and more patterns, from stripes to florals,” for styling a bed, she adds.

I’m not sure what’s left to say about this bedding brand that hasn’t already been plastered across subway ads or Instagram feeds, but in short, Brooklinen is somewhat of a bedding celebrity. It has garnered cool-kid status by offering top-quality products using Oeko-Tex-certified products at reasonable prices.

According to recent reports, the Classic Duvet Cover is made of percale, which can be compared to a crisp cotton button-down shirt. It’s soft and sophisticated in a matte, buttery finish that can be attributed to long-staple cotton fibers that are spun to make stronger but finer yarn.

We are not only big fans of Brooklinen products for their breathable, sustainable materials but also for their versatile designs. With 20 earthy tones, I recommend this duvet cover for any type of bedroom style—but I’d lean towards purchasing for a coastal design because of the soothing colors and prints.

Like Alpert, who has this duvet cover in her bedroom, I recommend styling it with textured linen sheets for a contrasting yet comfortable fabric combination and a throw blanket in complementary neutral and oceanic hues.

Not one but two AD writers love this Brooklinen cotton duvet cover all year long. Shopping writer Julia Harrison calls this super, super soft and very cool to the touch. “It stays cool even when I’ve wrapped myself all the way in it like a caterpillar so I’m never overheating, but I am staying comfy and warm,” she shares. Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert indicates this is her favorite duvet cover of all time, hands-down, because of its unmatched airy and parachute-like quality. “The percale duvet cover has this smooth feel but at the same time it is remarkably light and crisp,” she says. “Apparently, it’s all because of the high-quality single-ply yarns, which are made from strong, long-staple cotton fibers that give it that buttery touch.”.

In a recent development, the style potential is a plus here too. Alpert loves the “oyster” print since it strays away from more expected patterns like stripes filling up her linen closet. She got the matching sheets in the same print for this exact reason, saying the swirls remind her of “Hokusai’s waves and stand out in the sea of florals and plaids” in her linen closet.

In a recent development, from pajamas to sheets, Cozy Earth is a favorite of ours—and Oprah thanks to frequent appearances in her Favorite Things lists—for cooling bedding made of bamboo fabric. Its offerings also ring in at a budget-friendly price (especially with the brand’s frequent sales).

Many of the colors in Cozy Earth’s collection are grounded in the earth (to be expected). With this in mind, I see this duvet cover in a minimalist, bohemian, or coastal bedroom. Alpert’s peony pick is just as nice for a romantic bedroom or something seasonal for summer.

The delicate nature of the bedding (both in texture and color) makes it a striking contrast against crisp, patterned accents, like a percale floral sheet set.

When I asked Alpert what her favorite qualities are about Cozy Earth’s signature, silky duvet cover, there were almost too many to count. “This duvet cover is a trifecta of perks: It looks good, feels good, and won’t slip off the comforter,” she states. “But if I had to pick one, I’d say that I love the delicate pink hue and the equally delicate feel of the cover—just looking at my bed makes me want to crawl into it.”.

According to recent reports, the material (100% viscose from bamboo) has a breathable and smooth feel to it that’s nice for hot sleepers but also anyone who doesn’t want a more textured cover like linen. Even better, the soft, pastel-inspired color options like peony pink and laurel green make it a great fit for styling a bed during this blooming season. “The fabric is so delicate and dreamy that it reminds me of flower petals,” Alpert tells me. “Since I chose the peony colorway, it definitely fits the romantic profile.”.

According to recent reports, even though it has a smooth texture, the comforter inside won’t slip around because of the secure snap closures. “Cozy Earth has 12(!) points of contact between the comforter and the cover, so there is no way anything is going to get loose, especially because these are snapped on, and not tied, like many other duvet covers,” she says. “I pair it with the bamboo viscose comforter with standard fill and the combination works great because the comforter has some weight and the duvet cover does not mess with it in any way.”.

Sources indicate that A darling of the 2010s direct to consumer movement, Parachute is a home brand best known for its bedding, though the organization has also dabbled in furniture, mattresses, and other essentials. Its products, including the Linen Duvet Cover, are Oeko-Tex Standard 100–certified, meaning that every element (even buttons!) has been tested for substances damaging to human health. Parachute also doesn’t artificially soften their products. In the wrong hands, linen can be itchy or stiff until it’s been broken in, but that wasn’t the case here. This version, made of European Flax and made in the Guimarães region of Portugal, was inviting and oh so soft. The company also touts the material as naturally antimicrobial, which is a plus.

Another pick for a bohemian bedroom, this duvet cover has a lived-in look and several organic colors to choose from.

According to recent reports, if you, in true minimalist fashion, like a monochrome bedscape, style this duvet cover with linen sheets in natural colors. If you want a slightly moodier bedroom, try a shade like cacao or indigo.

Recent findings suggest that contributor Lila Allen has nothing but good things to say about the feel of this linen and its nonchalant elegance: “I was pleasantly surprised at how soft this cover was—with linen, sometimes it can be a roll of the dice. This set had the best of both worlds: super supple but still casually elevated. The linen is a nice thickness, too; I can’t see any trace of the duvet inside of it.” Parachute’s linen has 175 GSM, and Quince’s linen that I mention down below has around 150 GSM. To Allen’s point, this means Parachute’s is more durable with a substantial feel and less opaque (the reason why she can’t see her duvet insert peeking through) with a lighter cover color like toast or sand.

According to recent reports, allen pairs her duvet cover with an all-season comforter from Riley, which she indicates stays secure through a button closure on the side and gives just the right amount of rumple together. The insert moves around a bit inside of the cover but mostly remains in place. “Best of all, I’ve been sleeping soundly with the set on hot nights as well as ones where the AC has been on overdrive, and so far it holds up in both situations—not too warm or cool.” Allen tells me that she shares a bed with her “hot-blooded husband and a large Maine Coon cat,” so her bed usually runs warm. This layerable, snuggly cover is perfect.

Recent findings suggest that the home brand is headquartered in Fresh York City, however, the materials are sourced from fourth-generation, family-owned textile mills in Portugal and other countries across Europe. The products span a range of bedding and bath products, namely duvet covers, sheets, towels, mats, and other accessories like pillows and robs.

Since all of the duvet covers come in neutral, unfussy colors, this is a great option for minimalists.

Recent findings suggest that I style this simply with other neutrals like white or cream sheets. When I want to add more visual interest, I layer in butter yellow bedding or a quilt in soft, muted tones.

To put it simply, this duvet cover feels like a lightweight cashmere sweater. It’s not stuffy, but it’s not flimsy either. Riley Home’s somehow managed to make a cover that feels airy enough for nights when my apartment’s radiator runs overly hot and still warm enough when I want to curl up in bed after a cold commute from work.

Industry observers note that even though it feels soft, it’s not made of pure cashmere. In reality, it’s made of 95% cotton and just 5% cashmere, but I wouldn’t have noticed if I didn’t read the label so closely. The texture has a brushed quality to it that feels gentle and light on my skin. There are a few neutral colors on the site. I went with the oatmeal and have liked styling it with white sheet sets so far for a simple, not-overly-done-up bedspread. A couple of other thoughtful details are the interior ties and buttons to keep my comforter from shifting inside. The super-easy care sold me too. The brand doesn’t recommend dry cleaning—just a machine wash and dry with a gentle detergent will do. As someone who has lugged specialty cashmere bedding to NYC cleaners on foot through the years, this note in and of itself almost convinced me to give the bedding a try.

Quince’s entire deal is about making high-quality luxury products at an affordable price. They work only with factories that are both sustainable and pay a fair wage, which is something that many shoppers care enough about to pay a little extra for, but Quince cuts back on things like fancy packaging to keep costs down.

Quince is another AD favorite for its plethora of prints and solid colors. Try this duvet cover in your space—no matter its design style—for a lightweight addition to your bedscape that’s also budget friendly.

It has been revealed that since linen makes a statement on its own with its lived-in look, I recommend styling this duvet cover with Quince’s classic European linen sheet set and a fluffy duvet insert in moody neutral hues (think deep brown) for a cozy sleep oasis. It’s also neutral enough that you can add some pattern sheeting for extra personality.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve had this Quince linen duvet for about a year and it’s been a mainstay since it’s substantial and textured while still having an airiness to it—even when I’m layering with a few throw blankets or quilts when it’s cold outside. Sometimes linen gets a bad rap for its rough texture, but this best seller has been gentle against my skin and only gotten softer with more routine wear and care. It’s not as soft as something like an heirloom-quality stonewashed linen, but I’m not too picky in the linen department. I think its Oeko-Tex certification gives it a leg up generally to some competitors in this fabric category too.

According to recent reports, I chose this Quince duvet since there were so many color options to choose from. I love moody colors year-round, and the burgundy is true to the deep color I saw on the site and it hasn’t faded after months of washes. It has the relaxed look you know and love with linen materials. Steaming it knocks out wrinkles easily whenever I want a more put-together look in my bedroom, though.

Industry observers note that at this price point and with the most colors and prints available in this guide, I think this comforter cover can give you a great, budget-friendly way to dress a bed. The button closures also help keep a duvet insert or comforter in place. The care has been simple. I wash it with similar colors on a cold cycle and tumble dry on low and have only noticed a loose thread here and there, but nothing too crazy.

As mentioned above in our top overall pick, Brooklinen is known as the “home of the internet’s favorite sheets,” so we find it to be a worthy destination for quality bedding—including this quilt-like duvet cover made with 100% cotton.

With a design that mirrors the appearance of a quilt, we think this duvet cover would dress a vintage-inspired space beautifully—like the bedding you’d find in a historic Victorian home.

Alpert chose the plum colorway because of its sophisticated look that anchors her bedroom. She shares that the hue looks exceptionally well-paired with the deep caramel of the Boll & Branch Grand waffle blanket, as the color almost works like a moody neutral.

Even though the Brooklinen website describes this duvet as “breezy,” Alpert states it feels more like a weighted blanket. “The ribbed side is certainly quilt-like, which is not surprising because each ribbon that runs through the duvet cover is padded ever so slightly,” she shares.

Sources indicate that the cover has a two-sided design: one side with textured, ribbed matelasse and the other with a crisp percale fabric. Alpert thinks this material combo is genius since it keeps the duvet cover from feeling too heavy. “This is especially key for anyone who sleeps without a flat sheet—you’ll feel like you’re getting into freshly changed linens night after night,” she says. “On the flip side, the ribbed texture elevates the duvet cover, not only in how it looks but it gives your bedding a slightly cushy sensation.”.

Industry observers note that rest assured that the feel isn’t as heavy as an actual weighted blanket. Alpert says it certainly has substance and structure, though. “When I sleep with it on, it feels as if I am very secure—no one will dare wake me up,” she notes.

Hommey is a relatively new Australian-based brand that got its start in 2020. It became popular for robes and nightwear in bold, fashionable stripes. The designs are now spread across the bedding category, including cotton and linen sheets and duvet covers.

Since the brand is known for more out-of-the-box colorways across its collections, this duvet color is a great option for maximalists looking to experiment with bold color-blocking.

For a moodier bedscape, I style this duvet cover with sheets in a deep tone like burgundy. Overall, the chocolatey hue acts like a neutral and pairs beautifully with lighter sheet colors like oatmeal, which can also complement the cream-colored trim.

I know we’ve talked about linen a couple of times already in this story, but Hommey’s duvet helps hit the trifecta for the category. The natural flax fiber felt smoother and more broken-in than my Quince version right out the package. My guess is that it’s because of the stonewashed finish, which is known to give scratchy linen a more silky quality. I won’t get ahead of myself and say it feels like pure silk, but I can confirm that it’s soft and breathable almost like an organic cotton duvet after a few washes. The duvet caught my attention even more because of all of the styles. There are over 30 fashionable colors and prints, like the oxford and plum reversible cotton duvet I want in a button-down shirt version. The linen offering has four distinct colorways, including the brown sugar with cream trim that I got for myself. I like deep colors for my bedscape, especially as the year starts inching towards fall and winter, and its rich hue hasn’t disappointed. It's the perfect complement to my autumnal color palette, especially when I pair it with burgundy linen sheets.

It is less expensive than the Parachute pick and has a plusher texture than the Quince, so I’d say this is the perfect middle ground for an approachable but high-quality linen duvet.

Garnet Hill was founded in Fresh Hampshire in the mid-1970s by Pegge and Grant Dowse who built the brand on a commitment to sustainable materials, thoughtful craftsmanship, and responsible sourcing with products like organic cotton and flannel bedding. The bedding blends traditional styles with a modern touch to fit in a range of bedrooms.

Recent findings suggest that our tester says the Pear Garden print is completely unexpected. “As much as I love florals, stripes, and gingham, a girl needs a break…and these charming pears are just the right motif,” Alpert shares. “They signal a cottagecore moment without going over the top. Every time I glimpse the cheery yellow fruit, I crack a little smile. Plus, the colorway of bold yellow, sage green, brown, and cream are easy to coordinate with the rest of my bedding collection.”.

Because the pear motifs are the statement, we think you can go with more subtle sheets like a white set with embroidered trim. If you’re more of a maximalist, you can lean into the pattern play with a gingham sheet set in a complementary muted tone like brown and extra layers like a faux fur blanket if you’re cozying up for winter.

In a recent development, according to Alpert, this duvet cover is synonymous with cozy. It’s the softest option on this list because of the brushed flannel fabric, and it’s also a great pick if you live in cold climates since it has a bit of heft to it. “It’s as if a layer of leaves, or in this case pears, is surrounding me during winter hibernation,” she states. “That’s in part because this specific flannel is woven to have a substantial six-ounce weight.”.

In a recent development, alpert’s had this for nearly one year and says it has a decadent texture, likening it to climbing under a layer of meringue when she pairs it with her fluffy Ostermoor down duvet insert. “The plush feel of the cover also makes me think that I’ve just scored an upgrade to a royal suite,” Alpert adds.

At this point, she hasn’t noticed any pilling, but she does note that the cover is a bit snugger than a typical king, so you can expect the duvet to feel a little loftier than a regular fit.

What to Look for in the Best Duvet Covers.

Industry observers note that A duvet cover is more than just a bedcover. This eye-catching textile has a large footprint in any bedroom and can instantly give your space a refresh—whether with unique colors and prints or something more modest—especially if you want to disguise an old duvet insert. With this in mind, I tapped AD PRO Directory designers to weigh in on what to look for in a duvet cover to elevate your bedroom.

Material: When it comes to duvet covers, everyone has their own personal preferences. For Nicole R. Fisher, CEO and founder of Nicole Fisher Interiors, it’s linen: “They’re effortless, lightweight, and airy. I think the simplicity of the linen transcends different styles and spaces,” she indicates. Fisher notes that the feel is a major factor when selecting a duvet cover.

Carmen René Smith, founder and principal designer of Aquilo Interiors, states that it also needs to feel soft to the touch, breathable, and cozy. “What’s the point of a beautiful duvet if you don’t want to snuggle into it?” she says. “Texture is key too—whether it’s silky, crisp, or nubby, it should add depth to the space.”.

Comfort: All of the interior designers I spoke to for this story point to natural fibers, not only because of their quality but also their airflow and breathability. Shelbie Cox of Shelbie Cox Studio recommends natural fibers like organic cotton and linen and notes that polyester and other synthetic fibers are best to avoid since they can trap heat.

Industry observers note that design: With so many patterns and colors to choose from, it’s important to keep your bedroom’s design style in mind. If you like more of a minimalist bedroom, Cox suggests a fine stripe pattern (like Quince’s European Linen Duvet Cover) or a monochromatic, muted color palette (see the Cozy Earth Bamboo Duvet Cover) for your duvet cover set.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to go bold for your bedroom, there are options aplenty. “We’re maximalists, so we say bump up the color and pattern no matter what your signature style is!” says Smith, adding that it’s important to still maintain balance. “If you have bold wallpaper, pull a color from it and go for a solid, textured duvet—like a rich velvet for drama or a soft linen for a more relaxed vibe. If you’re mixing patterns, think about scale—a bold, oversized print pairs best with a smaller, more delicate duvet pattern to give the eye a place to rest.”.

Recent findings suggest that if you don’t want to commit to one style just yet, rest assured that having a few duvets in rotation can help you keep your bedroom design fresh. “I tend to go simple on bedding and let the accessories be the pops of pattern and color that’s easily swapped out,” adds Fisher.

Maintenance: While these are great design accessories for a bedroom, they also need to be practical. Ashley Ross, founder and principal designer of Muse Noire Interiors recommends keeping these questions in mind when shopping: How does it fasten (zipper, tie up, or buttons)? Does it fit within your washer and dryer? This will help you know how to use it and how to care for it.

How We Tested the Best Duvet Covers.

We tested the best duvet covers the same way we test products for the rest of our sleep content: by bringing the items in our homes and dressing them on our beds. This way, you’re guaranteed to get a real-life look at how the products perform after weeks and months of everyday use. We also wash them routinely to keep an eye out for any wear and tear. All of the brands we feature reflect a variety of price points, designs, and materials so you have the best options to choose from for your bedroom.

Jump to the “How We Tested” section of this article to watch an in-depth video about our testing methodology and some of our favorite products and brands.

Do I Really Need a Duvet Cover?

In a recent development, you don’t necessarily need a duvet cover. It depends on how you like to dress your bed. In my opinion, it’s a great bed accessory. A duvet cover not only protects your duvet insert but it also gives you the opportunity to easily switch up your bedscape (instead of swapping comforters when you want a new look). That stated, pay attention to the care instructions for your insert because some do not recommend washing or dry cleaning.

There are several ways you can put a duvet cover on, but according to TikTok experts, this method below is as foolproof as possible:.

Start by turning your duvet cover inside out, top side down, with the duvet opener at the foot of the bed. Then, place your comforter on top and secure the corners with the attached ties to the duvet cover. Starting at the head of the bed, roll the duvet down towards the foot just like a burrito. Finally, fold the duvet opening over each end of the roll, and unroll the blanket back towards the.

Industry observers note that always check the manufacturer instructions to find out how to wash your specific duvet cover. However, the most common way to clean a duvet cover is by machine washing it with like colors with a gentle detergent on a cold cycle. If the duvet cover has a zipper closure, it's usually helpful to zip it closed to keep it from snagging in the washing machine.

How Often Should You Wash a Duvet Cover?

Industry observers note that it's generally recommended to wash your duvet cover as often as you wash your sheets, which is about once a week. If you use a top sheet, though, you can usually extend another week and wash your duvet cover every other week.

How Did AD Pick Products to Test?

Our editors selected top products in this story from tried-and-true brands on the market, from Brooklinen to Boll & Branch. These brands boast organic materials like 100% organic cotton and European Flax and bamboo for a sustainably made bed. Plus, many boast eco-friendly certifications like GOTS and Oeko-Tex so you know they are free of chemicals. As a design editor, I also made sure all of the products have a range of colors, patterns, and prints to complement a bedroom’s style.

“We Need to Change Our Management”: Ricardo Salinas on Mexico’s Future, Bukele and Bitcoin

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1980 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • •       Mexico: Salinas called Mexico’s political class “despicable” and said “I’m working on that,” pointing to 2030, when the presidency is “up for grabs.”.
  • •       El Salvador: “They’re growing very fast here,” he said, crediting “the changes that Bukele has put in place.”.
  • •       United States: America’s welfare-warfare state is “alive and well,” with Washington “borrowing like a drunken sailor.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

•       Mexico: Salinas called Mexico’s political class “despicable” and said “I’m working on that,” pointing to 2030, when the presidency is “up for grabs.”.

•       El Salvador: “They’re growing very fast here,” he said, crediting “the changes that Bukele has put in place.”.

•       United States: America’s welfare-warfare state is “alive and well,” with Washington “borrowing like a drunken sailor.”.

•       Bitcoin: “The last 12 months have been hell for Bitcoiners,” but it’s not over, as long as you can “take the blow.”.

•       Banking: Paraguay’s crisis exposed “the original sin of banking”: borrowing short and lending long.

In an interview with Ricardo Salinas Pliego, the Mexican billionaire behind Grupo Salinas and one of Bitcoin’s most outspoken advocates in Latin America, recorded at Bitcoin Histórico in El Salvador this week, we discovered his views on Mexico’s political future, Bukele’s El Salvador, America’s debt spiral, and why he believes Bitcoin’s toughest year changes nothing.

Speaking in San Salvador’s National Palace on You’re The Voice podcast, Salinas didn’t hold back.

It has been revealed that asked about the biggest challenges facing Mexico, Salinas started with the country’s potential. “We’re 130 million Mexicans,” he said, plus another 40 million of Mexican origin living in the United States, who send home “$5 billion a month in remittances. We call that love.” Half of Mexico’s population, he added, is under 30.

But what’s holding Mexico back?

“We have a problem: the terrible management that we have, the terrible government that we have. The political class is despicable. They’re incapable. They’re corrupt. They lie all the time. So we need to change our management. And I’m working on that.”.

Asked whether he intends to be part of that change, Salinas drew a line between two fronts. On “the battle of ideas, what we call the cultural battle,” he said, “I’m all in.” The electoral battle is different: “The electoral battle has timing, it has windows, and it has rules, and I don’t set them.”.

He then laid out the calendar. In June 2027, Mexico elects its entire lower house of Congress and 18 of its 32 governors. In 2030, “we have everything up for grabs: the Congress, the Senate, the presidency, and the other 18 governors.”.

Industry observers note that “So it’s going to be interesting in ’30,” he remarked. “But from here to there, it’s a long time, huh? We’ll take it one day at a time.”.

The night before the interview, Salinas joined a group of Bitcoin Histórico speakers at a dinner with President Nayib Bukele. In a lighthearted moment, Bukele poked fun at himself, recalling how he had rushed to make El Salvador the first country to adopt Bitcoin, convinced other nations were about to beat him to it. Looking back, he found it funny.

Ricardo Salinas and President Nayib Bukele | Credit: Casa Presidencial.

Ricardo Salinas and President Nayib Bukele | Credit: Casa Presidencial.

It has been revealed that “And it didn’t happen, right? He was the only one that did it,” Salinas noted. “So these things take time. There’s a lot of entrenched interest in the financial world and in government circles that do not want to see the end of fiat. Because fiat, what I call the fiat fraud, is what enables all the spending, right? And if you live off of that, you don’t want it to stop.”.

Industry observers note that salinas pointed to El Salvador’s unusual position: its currency is the U.S. dollar, which it cannot print. “So Bukele was saying last night, ‘I’m not in charge of the inflation.'”.

Recent findings suggest that salinas is bullish on the country’s direction. “They’re growing very fast here,” he noted, adding that he expects El Salvador to “do much better, with the changes that Bukele has put in place.” As for the criticism the country faces, he was dismissive: “You have to take things from who they come from.”.

Bitcoin Historico 2026 speakers at President Bukele’s Dinner | Credit: Casa Presidencial.

In a 2022 interview with Max Keiser and Stacy Herbert, Salinas argued that fiat money has allowed the “big state” to exist, funding both the warfare state and the welfare state. Four years later, he says nothing has changed, and the United States is the prime example.

According to recent reports, “The United States is the maximum example of the welfare-warfare state. The exceptionalism of the United States is that they get to print the reserve currency of the world.”.

Citing the Cantillon effect, the Austrian School idea that newly created money reaches some people before others, Salinas remarked the first in line are “all these defense contractors and the warfare state,” followed by welfare programs such as Medicaid and hospitals.

“So I think the welfare-warfare state is alive and well,” he said. By his count, U.S. debt has climbed from around $25 trillion to $40 trillion over the past four years, “and there’s no end in sight. They’re not going to stop.”.

It has been revealed that he described Washington as “borrowing like a drunken sailor” and warned that rising interest payments will squeeze everything else. “The amount of interest that the US government is going to have to pay on this debt is huge, and it’s going to leave very little money for all the rest of the stuff, including defense and welfare.”.

Salinas didn’t sugarcoat the past year. “The last 12 months have been hell for Bitcoiners,” he mentioned. “That’s the title of my talk: ‘Is It Over for Bitcoin?'”.

His answer is no. “But you have to be able to take the blow. And not many people are able to take the blow, because it’s much more psychological than financial.”.

For Salinas, price swings don’t touch the core thesis. “Governments are borrowing much more than they should, they’re spending much more than they should, and that’s causing the debasement of the currency. And that’s stealing from people’s pockets. Period. And we’re all being victims of this.”.

He also took aim at conventional portfolio advice. The traditional 60% stocks, 40% bonds split for young investors is, in his words, “really bad advice. It’s self-serving, by the financial industry.” That, he mentioned, “is where investing in Bitcoin comes in.”.

Ricardo Salinas speaking at Bitcoin Historico 2026, El Salvador | Credit: Bitcoin Historico.

The interview came days after Paraguay’s central bank took over the digital lender Ueno Bank, freezing depositors’ access to their money, and the country’s Senate voted to remove President Santiago Peña from office over the crisis. Peña, who held shares in Ueno’s parent tech giant until last year, has denied wrongdoing.

In a recent development, for Salinas, whose Grupo Salinas owns Banco Azteca, the collapse exposed a flaw built into every bank on earth. “The original sin of banking, is borrowing short and lending long.”.

Recent findings suggest that depositors believe their money is available on demand, he explained, but the bank lends it out for car loans, mortgages and office buildings with longer maturities. “All the banks in the world, in every country, operate the same way. They borrow short and they lend long, so they always have a liquidity problem. Always.” The fix would be full reserve banking, he noted, “but there are no full reserve banks in the world today.”.

He remarked Paraguay’s case combined that structural flaw with bad decisions, and that “the more serious accusation is that the owners of the bank were using the assets of the bank for their own purposes, outside of the regulatory framework.”.

According to recent reports, salinas called Peña “a good leader,” while adding he doesn’t know how involved the president was. He warned of the political fallout: “All the left-wingers are celebrating the demise and the fall of Santiago Peña, and populism is increasing its calls for more government intervention, more spending.”.

It has been revealed that on reports that pension money was held at the bank, he was blunt about government promises, which he mentioned “are usually worth nothing.” Pension pools, he added, are a tempting target: “Governments love to put their hands on other people’s money. It’s a great target. And I think that’s what happened in Paraguay.”.

For Salinas, the next generations are the ones paying for their elders’ promises. Before Mexico’s 1997 pension reform, he remarked, the government was “taking taxes from young people to pay the pensions of the old people. That’s a really bad deal for young people.”.

He sees it as a symptom of a deeper problem: “this wrong idea that the government is like a parent.” In Asia and Latin America, he said, “the family is the life raft of people. Because you cannot trust the government.” In Europe and the United States, “people have been made to believe that they can trust the government, and it’s wrong.”.

A father of six and grandfather of ten, Salinas described his own pact simply: “I’m going to try to leave them a better place than the one I found.”.

It has been revealed that he made his point with a provocative analogy: “So what happens in a family where the mother is a prostitute and the father is a drunk? What kind of family is going to come out of that? Well, nothing good, right?” The West, he argued, has been “deceived into thinking that some bureaucrats are going to take care of these children. They’re not.”.

“That is the treason of the intergenerational pact,” he said. “It’s very serious. And that manifests itself in taking on debt, wars, spending, student loans…” His answer for young people starts with education: “Find out what they’re doing to your future. Find out what they’re doing to your money.” Next comes what he calls “the tax bite.” By his estimate, the government takes about 47% of labor income in Mexico and 60% in France, versus just 5% in Guatemala. “Don’t let the government steal the product of your work.”.

Ricardo Salinas and Efrat Fenigson at El Salvador’s National Palace | Credit: Bitcoin Historico.

It has been revealed that salinas also revealed he is looking at investments in the Dominican Republic, which he called “a well-managed country” with a successful focus on tourism and agriculture. Its neighbor got a harsher verdict: “Haiti is a basket case for governance and democracy.”.

Sources indicate that but he sees hope coming from El Salvador. Bukele recently deployed more than 2,000 Salvadoran troops to Haiti, and Salinas welcomed the move, describing it as “sending in 2,000 troops to put down the gangs. I think it’s a great start in the right direction.”.

Industry observers note that the Dominican Republic’s big problem, he mentioned, is energy, since it has to import it. One option he has explored is small nuclear power plants, though President Luis Abinader is wary of the impact on tourism. Salinas disagrees. “You can’t have tourism if you don’t have energy, right? You need a lot of energy.”.

It has been revealed that asked what keeps him optimistic, Salinas described a cycle he believes drives prosperity: freedom leads to creativity, success gets copied, and copying leads to improvement. “Copy, improve. Copy, improve. And that is what leads to prosperity.”.

Industry observers note that the obstacle, as always in his view, is the state. “They cut down on freedom. They cut down on innovation through regulation. They cut down on competition through all these protectionist and crony laws, right? And then they take the product from people’s hands and mouths and spend it on stupid things.”.

According to recent reports, his prescription is simple: “It’s freedom, innovation, competition, prosperity. Small, very small government, for law and order and defense. That’s it.”.

Libertarian values, an Austrian economist’s grasp of money, a Bitcoiner’s conviction and a patriarch’s devotion to family: Salinas has made his recipe clear. What Mexico will find out by 2030 is whether he intends to serve it himself.

Choose one accented with velvet ribbons for a touch of nostalgia, or opt for something that looks as though it was plucked straight from a whimsical snowscape, complete with pinecones and berries. And if you’ve historically never considered yourself a “wreath person,” take this as your sign to make this the year you become one. Turns out, participating in holiday cheer is just as delightful as it sounds.

While you may turn to Quince for an affordable cashmere sweater or linen bedding, the unsung treasures might surprise you. Take this faux foliage wreath, for instance, which mimics the look and feel of a Norfolk pine so convincingly, you’d never know the difference from the street. Simple and full, its bare branches make the perfect backdrop for trailing red bows, tinsel, or whatever other accoutrements you desire.

In short, it’s designed with durability in mind to outlast wintry weather and beyond. It'll also keep you from sweeping a single pine needle off your front porch (a gift in itself).

According to recent reports, if evergreens, real or fake, aren't your thing, we say go full color. This Lulu and Georgia wreath is made of velvety baubles, each with a plush texture and rich hue. It's the perfect size for hanging from a cabinet, chair back, or interior door when you want to add a simple but effective holiday touch.

Something to make your days merry and bright, literally. This faux wreath comes pre-lit, saving you the hassle of weaving your own lights through the branches (and sparing you any DIY allegations). With softly draping cedar branches and a warm white glow, it makes an inviting addition to front doors, mantels, and more.

Industry observers note that there's something especially charming about holiday decorations that look as though they've been gathered on a winter walk. Hang it on your front door or prop it on a mantel for a dose of old-fashioned holiday spirit.

A few perfectly placed pinecones can make a wreath feel understated yet exceptionally sophisticated. The real-touch greenery is convincing enough to have guests wondering when you found the time to forage a Noble Fir yourself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s luxury brand, Denza, calls it “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles.” The upcoming Denza N8 electric SUV will launch next week, offering an impressive CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles), massive digital screens, and plenty of premium extras.

After opening pre-orders for the fresh 5-seat luxury electric SUV last week, Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, said the results so far “have been excellent.”.

According to Li, the Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year.” Using BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries, the Denza N8 EV has a pure electric CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) on a single charge.

That’s just as much as the N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

While Li confirmed last week that the upcoming EV variant would go on sale in November, he didn’t give a specific date.

Now, it’s official. Denza announced on its Weibo page on Friday that the launch event for the Denza N8 EV will be held on November 12, 2026.

BYD is still offering a limited-time promo that includes a 5,000 RMB credit for those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit.

According to recent reports, the Denza N8 measures 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase. That’s slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

Industry observers note that it’s available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).

The tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).

Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will use either a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) and 800 km (497 miles), respectively.

It has been revealed that the Denza N8 also features BYD’s latest Flash Charging technology, letting it recharge from 10% to 80% in just five minutes. It takes just nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a fresh 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.

Like most of its upcoming luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is loaded with BYD’s latest software and technology.

Added premium features include zero-gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.

The electric SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system, plus its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system.

BYD has yet to announce prices for the Denza N8 EV, but it will likely be slightly less than the N8L, an extended version that starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000).

Russia Lets Everyday Investors Buy Bitcoin Starting Today

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everyday investors in Russia can legally buy bitcoin through regulated brokers and crypto exchange offices starting Tuesday, but two of the country’s biggest retail brokers, T-Bank and VTB, are not offering it yet.
  • In a recent development, the Bank of Russia ordinance that took effect Nov.
  • Retail buyers can purchase through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everyday investors in Russia can legally buy bitcoin through regulated brokers and crypto exchange offices starting Tuesday, but two of the country’s biggest retail brokers, T-Bank and VTB, are not offering it yet.

In a recent development, the Bank of Russia ordinance that took effect Nov. 17 approves bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, the legal term for ordinary retail buyers who do not meet Russia’s wealth or experience thresholds. From the same date, exchanges may admit those three assets to public trading.

Retail buyers can purchase through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary are capped at 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the central bank’s official rate on Tuesday. The cap applies per intermediary, not per person.

Qualified investors face no cap and can access any crypto asset. Every buyer, regardless of status, must pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before the first trade.

JUST IN: 🇷🇺 Starting today, Russian retail investors can now legally buy Bitcoin 👀 pic.twitter.com/EzifKUtcea.

Industry observers note that the legal door opened before the apps did. “The main reason T-Bank clients do not yet see cryptocurrencies in their banking app is the absence of a market standard for testing,” Alexander Kretov, head of blockchain technology development at T-Bank, told TASS on Tuesday. “As soon as the Bank of Russia publishes it on its official website, we are ready to launch external operations.”.

Kretov mentioned T-Bank’s crypto exchange office and digital depository are built and in the final stages of live testing, and that the service will roll out in several stages, “starting with the most active users.”.

VTB’s brokerage arm told the agency it is testing the customer journey in its VTB My Investments app and is waiting for the remaining regulations. Once those land, it intends to open crypto trading first to qualified investors who pass the test. The central bank added VTB to its registries of digital depositories and crypto exchangers in October, and the broker ran its first crypto trades for corporate clients the same month.

In a recent development, the single test that brokers are waiting on has been drafted by two industry groups, NEXUS and NAUFOR. As of Nov. 10, the draft had been sent to the Bank of Russia for approval as part of a basic investor-protection standard, but it had not been approved. NAUFOR won self-regulatory status for crypto exchanges and digital depositories in October.

Recent findings suggest that tuesday’s rule is the first of several dates on Russia’s calendar. A separate central bank ordinance lets exchanges open organized crypto trading from Nov. 22, once the regulator has approved their trading rules. Moscow Exchange, the country’s largest venue, has stated it aims to start bitcoin, ether and USDT trading on Dec. 1, initially as a pilot. The exchange and its clearing house are under U.S. sanctions.

The central bank remarked it limited the retail list to the most liquid assets, judged by market capitalization, average daily trading volume and at least five years of pricing history on foreign exchanges. “This approach protects non-qualified investors from significant losses during sharp and unpredictable price swings,” the regulator said when it unveiled the list on Nov. 6, as quoted by *Kommersant*.

According to recent reports, russian buyers are not new to bitcoin. They already trade heavily on offshore platforms, Dmitry Lesnov, Finam’s deputy CEO for brokerage, told *Vedomosti*, which reported his estimate that Russia accounts for 15% to 20% of traffic on the largest Asian crypto exchanges. Lesnov also said the 300,000-ruble cap will significantly limit retail interest, and that some buyers will likely stay on foreign exchanges, non-custodial wallets and decentralized platforms.

According to recent reports, the framework rests on Federal Law No. 282-FZ, “On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights,” whose main provisions took effect Sept. 1. It licenses exchanges, brokers and depositories but still bans using crypto to pay for goods and services inside Russia.

The question now is less whether Russia allows retail bitcoin buying, and more how long the testing standard takes and whether the first apps can pull buyers home from the offshore desks they already use.

Tech Report: EVgo opens its first Tesla Superchargers, with hundreds more planned

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (504 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot.
  • The 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue.
  • It has been revealed that the Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot. The site has 12 fast-charging stalls with both NACS and CCS plugs, and it’s the first of hundreds of Tesla Supercharger stalls EVgo prepares to add across the US.

The 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue. EVgo’s August announcement cited up to 500 kW for the Supercharger rollout.

It has been revealed that the Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter. Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station indicates up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.

“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” stated Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.

It has been revealed that EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.

Smart move on EVGo's part. More reliable charger at a lower cost than they can build themselves, and Tesla takes on all the maintenance and network operations for a slice of the sales.

EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The manufacturer aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. Over the next two years, it aims to put at least one NACS plug at every EVgo site built in 2023 or later.

Industry News: Artists Helen Marden and the Late Brice Marden Refashioned a Decommissioned 19th-Century Ferry Terminal

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the course of their more than 50-year marriage, artist Helen Marden and her late husband, the eminent painter Brice Marden, amassed an international collection of seriously eccentric—and deeply magical—houses, gardens, and studios, each designed around the double helix of art and family.
  • Recent findings suggest that helen Marden in the living room.
  • It has been revealed that the living room includes chairs by Marcel Wanders (far left) and the Campana Brothers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the course of their more than 50-year marriage, artist Helen Marden and her late husband, the eminent painter Brice Marden, amassed an international collection of seriously eccentric—and deeply magical—houses, gardens, and studios, each designed around the double helix of art and family. They bought their first house, a cliffside cottage on the Greek island of Hydra, in 1973, and since then real estate and art have been entwined in their life, art facilitating the purchase of property, the properties both catalyst and carapace for the evolution of their art. An Italianate villa in upstate Upcoming York, a pair of traditional riads in Marrakech, a hotel set among the ruins of a 19th-century sugar plantation in the Caribbean, a second house by the port in Hydra, a Renaissance Revival town house in Manhattan, a stately manse on a sprawling estate in Pennsylvania—every one of their idiosyncratic properties has its own fascinating history, reflected in its interior. The homes are all documented in the upcoming book Brice & Helen Marden: Houses, Gardens, Studios (Gagosian), edited by this writer, with photography by Stephen Kent Johnson.

Recent findings suggest that helen Marden in the living room. Chair and side table by the Campana Brothers. The chimney is clad in Clé Tile. A watercolor by Henri Michaux rests on the mantel.

It has been revealed that the living room includes chairs by Marcel Wanders (far left) and the Campana Brothers. Sculpture at right by Michael Wang.

In the dining room, a Paavo Tynell pendant hangs above a rustic farm table with chairs by Jonathan Olivares and Maarten Baas. Amazonia marble covers one wall.

The Mardens were instinctively drawn to residences with endurance, places that have seen a few things, not newly built pleasure domes devoid of texture and soul. Swan House, the riparian hideaway in the middle of the Hudson River, epitomizes the couple’s embrace of the strange and the enchanted. Accessed by a long, narrow causeway that leads off the shore of Saugerties, the structure was built in 1877 as part of Long Dock, a ship terminal and moorage for large vessels conveying people and goods the length of the Hudson. It was also a landing for ferries crossing the river between Saugerties and the village of Tivoli. One can see Swan House shimmering in the landscape from the edge of Rose Hill, the Marden family’s 19th-century Tivoli estate.

Industry observers note that the Depression, along with the advent of more efficient modes of transport, scuppered the last of the large ships landing at Long Dock in the early 1930s, but ferries continued to make the two-minute trip across the water until 1938. After that, the structure was decommissioned from professional service and sold, becoming the only privately owned peninsula on the Hudson. The Mardens purchased the property in 2011, but it took a full decade before they engaged designer Daniel Sachs and architect Kevin Lindores of the AD100 firm Sachs Lindores Architecture, Interiors to execute a full-scale renovation.

The primary bath features custom zellige tiles, a vintage Vistosi chandelier, an antique marble sink, and a tub by The Water Monopoly.

According to recent reports, sachs Lindores remodeled the entry with a windscreen of glass brick. The chair is by Gaetano Pesce.

It has been revealed that yellow zellige tiles meet a pale pink Aga range beneath a custom zinc hood in the kitchen. The pendant light is by Adolf Loos from WOKA.

Brice Marden’s For Helen – Valentine 2019 (2015–18) hangs on the black-tiled fireplace tower that mediates the bedroom and living room.

A custom bed is flanked by an antique French console table and a Charles Rohlfs hall chair. Lighting includes a Franz West chandelier and a floor lamp by Achille and Pier Giacomo Castiglioni.

“Early on we demolished a few walls to open up the views, but it was pretty raw. We’d just go over and watch the boats go by,” Helen recalls. “You have a completely different relationship with the river when you’re sitting in the middle of it.”.

Given the famously cultivated, idiosyncratic tastes of the homeowners, the collaboration between Sachs Lindores and their clients was unusually fertile. Together, they reimagined the derelict building as a trick box for trapping the natural light that bounces off the water on all sides, with reflective, lead-coated copper siding and a zinc roof on the exterior and fields of luminous plaster, tile, and marble within. “Helen never shies away from a bold gesture. At first, she told us to paint the house red, but when we presented the idea of a glistening metal-clad box with light dancing on the skin, she immediately went for it,” Sachs recalls. “Brice and Helen were very interconnected in their aesthetic tastes and decision making,” Lindores adds. “As you might imagine, they studied every paint color and trim detail.”.

Ruins of the 19th-century dock remain alongside the house.

It has been revealed that A guest room is outfitted with a Pierre Jeanneret daybed, lounge chairs by Monika Mulder for IKEA, a vintage Kevin Walz standing lamp, and a Mathieu Matégot magazine rack. Painting by Helen Marden.

Sigmar Polke’s Untitled (1998) hangs above a vintage Walter Knoll sofa in the first-floor sitting room.

Sources indicate that while retaining the shape of its original architectural envelope, the house was essentially rebuilt, with newly introduced window configurations, open circulation, and an exposed ceiling, all in service of maximizing watery vistas and ease of use. On the lofty upper level, the existing chimney, newly revealed in its full floor-to-ceiling height, was clad in glossy black brick tile. The monolithic form now feels like a high altar in a temple of light. Custom zellige tiles imported from Fez cover the walls of the kitchen and baths, where Helen’s genius for juxtaposing colors and materials comes into high relief.

Recent findings suggest that the polyglot ensemble of furnishings hews closely to the signature Marden mix: Moroccan rugs; bold contemporary designs by the likes of Gaetano Pesce, Marcel Wanders, and the Campana Brothers; humble American folk pieces; 20th-century classics by Paavo Tynell, Adolf Loos, and Pierre Jeanneret; and a few Continental antiques to leaven the brew. “I just pick things that I like, things that make me happy,” Helen says, pooh-poohing the idea of some grand decorative vision. Her designers would demur. “She has an incredible eye,” Sachs insists. “The more crazy Helen would get, the more Brice liked it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Hyundai IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in America outside of Tesla, but its larger three-row sibling looks like the better deal right now.
  • Through September, the Hyundai IONIQ 5 was the third top-selling EV in the US, behind the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.
  • Hyundai’s electric SUV is outselling rivals like the Chevy Equinox EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, and Toyota bZ.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hyundai IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in America outside of Tesla, but its larger three-row sibling looks like the better deal right now.

Through September, the Hyundai IONIQ 5 was the third top-selling EV in the US, behind the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.

Hyundai’s electric SUV is outselling rivals like the Chevy Equinox EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, and Toyota bZ.

Industry observers note that why? For one, it’s one of the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at about $35,000, and Hyundai has been offering some of the most attractive lease deals.

After the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired at the end of September last year, Hyundai responded by reducing prices on the IONIQ 5 by up to nearly $10,000 on some trims.

The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250. That’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model adds $2,500, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, starts at $58,955, or nearly $24,000 more than the base IONIQ 5 SE.

Industry observers note that on Hyundai’s website, the 2027 IONIQ 5 SE Standard Range is available to lease from $359 a month. The offer is for a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing for an effective cost of $567 per month.

The extended-range Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE RWD can be leased from $369 a month. The offer is also a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing, for an effective cost of $577 per month.

It has been revealed that hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9, meanwhile, is available to lease from $419 a month. That deal also includes $4,999 due at signing, but is for a 36-month lease, so the effective cost is $557 per month.

Using Hyundai’s payment calculator, it would cost about $412 a month to lease the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE for 36 months with $4,999 due at signing. With an effective cost of $550 per month, it’s only $7 less than the three-row IONIQ 9.

The Hyundai IONIQ 9 offers more range than its smaller sibling, with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles for the base SE trim.

The IONIQ 5 is a midsize electric SUV, about the same size as a Tesla Model Y, with two rows and enough room for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating and six- or seven-seat configurations.

With an added row of seating, the IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with the IONIQ 5, which offers up to 106.5 cubic feet.

While the IONIQ 9 may be the better deal right now, the IONIQ 5 is still a good fit for those looking for a smaller, more efficient SUV that doesn’t necessarily need the added space.

Sources indicate that in comparison, the standard Tesla Model Y RWD is listed for lease starting at $499 a month with an EPA range of up to 321 miles. That’s for a 36-month lease with $3,000 down.

Using Tesla’s payment calculator, if you put the same $4,999 down for a 24-month lease like the IONIQ 5, the Model Y RWD’s monthly rate is $549.

Sources indicate that which one would you choose? The IONIQ 5, IONIQ 9, or Tesla Model Y? Let us know why in the comments.

Both the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are built at Hyundai’s Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

Industry observers note that I really haven’t seen much value in leasing. I’d rather buy the car outright using cash, with the goal of keeping the car for 10+ years.

My family recently bought a Hyundai IONIQ 5, and it is an outstanding car. Loaded with great features — both on the EV side and then for safety and comfort.

When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told us that its electric SUVs are attracting latest buyers to the brand at a higher rate than its gas or hybrid vehicles.

It has been revealed that the IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

Twenty One Capital (XXI) Buys 154 Bitcoin, Its First Purchase of 2026

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Twenty One Capital bought 154.32 bitcoin for about $10 million in cash after the weekend selloff, lifting its holdings to about 43,668 BTC.
  • Twenty One Capital bought 154.32 bitcoin for about $10 million in cash after the weekend selloff, the firm said Monday, its first disclosed purchase of 2026 and a small addition to a treasury that had barely moved all year.
  • It has been revealed that the Tether-controlled company stated it paid an average of about $64,801 per coin, bringing its holdings to about 43,668 BTC as of Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twenty One Capital bought 154.32 bitcoin for about $10 million in cash after the weekend selloff, lifting its holdings to about 43,668 BTC.

Twenty One Capital bought 154.32 bitcoin for about $10 million in cash after the weekend selloff, the firm said Monday, its first disclosed purchase of 2026 and a small addition to a treasury that had barely moved all year.

It has been revealed that the Tether-controlled company stated it paid an average of about $64,801 per coin, bringing its holdings to about 43,668 BTC as of Nov. 16. At Tuesday morning’s price near $64,900, that stack is worth roughly $2.83 billion.

Recent findings suggest that “Bitcoin is our benchmark for every investment decision we make. Any business we acquire has to beat simply buying more Bitcoin, and this weekend’s drop in price made adding Bitcoin an easy decision,” CEO Rapha Zagury remarked in the release.

“Every dollar we spend, whether on Bitcoin, acquisitions, or buybacks, is weighed against maintaining flexibility to run our business well,” he added.

Sources indicate that the buy breaks a long pause. Twenty One’s quarterly report, filed Nov. 13, shows it held 43,515 BTC at the end of 2025 and 43,514 BTC on Sept. 30. The only change in between was a single bitcoin transferred on March 31 as a vendor payment.

The same filing shows how much room the organization has to keep buying with cash. Twenty One reported $102.8 million in cash and equivalents at Sept. 30, down from $117.7 million at the end of 2025. The $10 million purchase equals about a tenth of that September balance, although the company has not noted how much cash it holds now.

Twenty One also carries $486.5 million of convertible notes issued when it went public. Those notes are secured by about 16,116 BTC pledged as collateral, coins the filing claims are not available for general corporate purposes while they back the debt.

Industry observers note that the tech giant’s bitcoin cost basis was about $3.69 billion at Sept. 30, or roughly $84,900 per coin. The fresh coins came in about $20,000 below that average, but the treasury as a whole remains underwater at current prices.

Twenty One’s Class A shares closed at $4.56 on Monday, down 7.9% on the day, before the purchase was revealed after the market close. The 10-Q lists 346.65 million Class A shares outstanding, which at that price are worth about $1.58 billion, well below the market value of the organization’s bitcoin.

That gap has been the central problem for Zagury since he replaced founder Jack Mallers as CEO in July. In an August shareholder letter, he acknowledged investor concerns about the stock trading at a discount to its bitcoin and mentioned Twenty One “must become more than a Bitcoin treasury.” Tether took control of the company in May after buying out SoftBank’s stake.

The organization’s latest shareholder letter, released Nov. 13 with third-quarter results, laid out a plan to build cash-generating businesses around the bitcoin treasury. Twenty One reported third-quarter net income of $1.087 billion, almost all of it from a $1.093 billion gain in the fair value of its bitcoin as prices rose during the quarter. For the first nine months of 2026, it posted a net loss of $186.5 million.

Twenty One said further bitcoin purchases are core to its strategy, with the amount and timing set by market conditions, available liquidity and competing investment opportunities. The organization did not commit to a size or schedule.

The purchase landed the same day Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder, disclosed buying 485 BTC for $33.4 million, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC.

The test now is whether those purchases stay opportunistic and small, or whether Twenty One uses bitcoin, acquisitions or buybacks to close the gap between its share price and its coins.

Apollo’s newest electric scooter is also its lowest-cost yet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market.
  • The newly introduced Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the company’s Black Friday sale running through November 30.
  • Sources indicate that the scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market. Now the tech giant is trying something different: going after the mass market with its least expensive model yet.

The newly introduced Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the company’s Black Friday sale running through November 30. More importantly, Apollo says the Dash isn’t intended to simply be a stripped-down budget scooter, but rather a way to bring much of its existing technology down to a lower price point.

Sources indicate that the scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). Its 480Wh battery is rated for up to 25 miles (40 km) of range in Eco mode.

Apollo also claims the 48V architecture avoids limiting motor power to anemic levels as the battery drains, meaning riders shouldn’t experience the same increasingly sluggish performance toward the bottom of the battery that can occur on some lower-cost scooters.

Recent findings suggest that at 43 lb (19.5 kg), the Dash is reasonably portable, though getting the weight and price down comes with an important compromise: there’s no suspension. Apollo also caps rider weight at 220 lb (100 kg), and points heavier riders or those regularly tackling rough roads and hills toward the more expensive Apollo Go instead.

Recent findings suggest that despite the lower price, there’s still a surprisingly long feature list. The Dash gets IP66 water resistance, self-healing tubeless tires, regenerative braking, built-in turn signals, Apollo’s Beam stem light, NFC unlocking, Apple Find My integration, and connectivity with the Apollo smartphone app.

According to recent reports, apollo claims it put the frame through 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of durability validation before shipping production units. A beta test program also accumulated 1,002 miles over 144 rides without any reported punctures or maintenance complications. Beta riders averaged 19 miles (30 km) per ride while finishing with 29% battery remaining, according to Apollo.

According to recent reports, perhaps the bigger story here, though, is where Apollo is positioning the Dash. The company says 52% of its customers previously owned scooters from brands including Segway, NIU, and Xiaomi, but historically moving up to an Apollo often meant crossing the $1,000 mark.

At $599, the Dash appears designed to get those riders into Apollo’s ecosystem much earlier – while also putting the organization squarely into competition with the mass-market scooters it previously sat above.

And for those wanting a bit more power or features, Apollo’s more upmarket models are on sale now as part of early Black Friday promotions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • He signed a record-breaking contract with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023, but where does Joe Burrow live when he’s not on the field?
  • Industry observers note that the NFL quarterback was born in Ames, Iowa, in 1996.
  • According to recent reports, it’s unsurprising, then, that Burrow has put down roots in the Buckeye State.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He signed a record-breaking contract with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023, but where does Joe Burrow live when he’s not on the field?

Industry observers note that the NFL quarterback was born in Ames, Iowa, in 1996. His family moved to Ohio when he was eight, and he has resided mostly in the Buckeye State ever since. Burrow played for Ohio State University from 2015 to 2017, then transferred as a graduate student to Louisiana State University, where he won the Heisman Trophy shortly before graduating in December 2019. He was drafted into the NFL the following year by his hometown Bengals, with whom he inked a $36.1 million, four-year contract—plus a $23.9 million signing bonus. Three years later Burrow signed a $275 million five-year extension, making him the highest-paid player in NFL history at the time, according to ESPN.

According to recent reports, it’s unsurprising, then, that Burrow has put down roots in the Buckeye State. Below, we’re examining the quarterback’s real estate portfolio.

Recent findings suggest that in May 2020, a month after being selected first overall in the NFL Draft, Burrow revealed that he was spending the pandemic lockdown in his old bedroom at his parents’ house in The Plains, Ohio, just outside of Athens. Interior design apparently wasn’t at the forefront of his mind; the room still had his childhood Star Wars curtains and posters on the wall, though he had given the bed a king-size upgrade in high school, replacing the Star Wars comforter that once rounded out the room’s theme. According to The Sun, the 1997-built residence sits on a cul-de-sac and has four bedrooms and three bathrooms.

The Bengals play at Paycor Stadium, formerly known as Paul Brown Stadium.

It has been revealed that in June 2020, Burrow spent $835,000 on his first house: a 2,900-square-foot Cincinnati dwelling just five miles from the Bengals’ home stadium. Located in the city’s historic Columbia-Tusculum area, the two-story property was built in 2014. Further details on the dwelling are scant—including whether or not Burrow still owns it. However, its location would make it a convenient place to stay during the NFL season.

According to recent reports, AD PRO members enjoy exclusive benefits. Get a year of unlimited access for $25 $20 per month.

Sources indicate that while we can’t confirm whether or not Burrow held onto his first property, we can be certain that he has since added on to his Ohio real estate portfolio in a big way. In 2023 the quarterback paid $7.5 million for a three-acre property near Coldstream Country Club, about 20 minutes from downtown Cincinnati. Not long after the purchase, a source told the Newly introduced York Post that Burrow was excited about the investment and planned to add a poolhouse to block outside views of the 7,300-square-foot main home, enhancing the residence’s privacy. Overlooking the Ohio River, the fully furnished 2014 build has four bedrooms and six bathrooms. It is located near the homes of two of Burrow’s teammates, Joe Mixon and Orlando Brown Jr., per the Post.

Industry observers note that in December 2024, Burrow’s residence was targeted by a group of thieves who stole an estimated $300,000 worth of goods from the house while he was in Dallas for an NFL game. Among the items taken were two diamond necklaces emblazoned with the athlete’s initials and jersey number. The burglary is believed to have happened during a security team shift change. Burrow’s girlfriend, model Olivia Ponton, was reportedly at the residence when the burglary happened and called 911, saying: “Someone broke into my house. It’s completely messed up.” The NFL star later made a statement about the unfortunate affair: “I feel like my privacy has been violated in more ways than one. And way more is already out there than I would want out there and that I care to share, so that’s all I got to say about that.” It seems Burrow has retained ownership of the property.

The QB’s contract with the Bengals extends through 2029, so he likely won’t be leaving Cincinnati any time soon.
